chunks: They said: 'We did not break our promise to you of our own will, but we were made to carry the loads of ornaments belonging to the people, which we threw (into the fire), and so did Sameri.'

key_terms.السَّامِرِيُّ: Al-Samiri (the individual who made the calf)

ai.seo_question: What did the Israelites say to Moses about their role in making the Golden Calf?
ai.summary: In this verse, the Israelites attribute their participation in the Golden Calf incident to the heavy burden of carrying the people's ornaments, a detail that highlights the psychological pressure of material wealth on faith. Shia exegesis often notes that Al-Samiri, the instigator, utilized these ornaments to create a calf that emitted a lowing sound, exploiting the Israelites' lingering attachment to idolatry during Moses' absence. This narrative serves as a cautionary tale against the corrupting influence of worldly adornments and the ease with which communities can revert to shirk when led by cunning figures.
